T17 Before N: (18,17), (18,23), (18,35), (24,41), (36,41)
T17 After N: (18,29), (18,35), (24,41), (36,41)
So N at (18,17) and (18,23) disappeared, and N at (18,29) appeared. Net: 5->4.
And G disappeared too!
This is interesting. When G was at (17,16)-(22,21) and I clicked (19,30):
- G disappeared
- N at (18,17) disappeared (was under G)
- N at (18,23) disappeared (was adjacent to G)
- N at (18,29) appeared (new position)
Wait, that doesn't quite make sense. Let me think again.
Actually, looking at T17, the action was MOUSE(19,30). The position (19,30) is in the center of the grid cell at (18,29)-(21,32). So clicking there:
- Moved G to (18,29)-(21,32)? No, G disappeared.
- Created a new N at (18,29)?
Hmm, let me reconsider. Maybe the mechanic is:
1. G is a "cursor" or "selector" that you can move by clicking
2. When G overlaps with an N token, clicking somewhere moves G and removes the overlapping N
3. The goal is to remove all N tokens by overlapping G with each one and clicking
But at T31, when G was at (17,34)-(22,39) and I clicked (19,24), ALL N tokens disappeared and G disappeared too. That's different from T17 where only some N tokens disappeared.
Let me check: at T31 before, G was at (17,34)-(22,39), which overlaps with N at (18,35)-(21,38). The other N tokens were at (18,29), (24,41), (36,41).
After T31, all N and G disappeared. This suggests that when G overlaps with an N token and you click somewhere, if certain conditions are met, all tokens are removed.
Wait, but at T17, G was at (17,16)-(22,21), which overlaps with N at (18,17)-(21,20). And after clicking (19,30), G disappeared and some N tokens changed.
Let me think about this differently. Maybe:
- Clicking on a grid cell moves G to that cell
- When G overlaps with N, the N token is "selected"
- Clicking again with G overlapping N removes that N token and moves G to a new position
- The goal is to remove all N tokens
But the T31 result is puzzling - all N tokens disappeared at once.
Let me look at the current state: G at (17,22)-(27,27), which overlaps with N at (18,23)-(21,26). I need to figure out what happens when I click with G overlapping an N token.
Actually, wait. Let me re-examine T17. The action was MOUSE(19,30), which is the center of the grid cell (18,29)-(21,32). This is an empty cell (no N token there before). After clicking:
- G disappeared
- N at (18,17) disappeared (was under G)
- N at (18,23) disappeared
- N at (18,29) appeared
So clicking on an empty cell when G overlaps with N:
1. Removes the N that was under G (and possibly adjacent Ns?)
2. Creates a new N at the clicked position
3. Removes G
This is getting complicated. Let me try a different approach - just try to reproduce the T31 winning sequence.
At T31, G was at (17,34)-(22,39) and clicking (19,24) removed everything.
Currently, G is at (17,22)-(27,27). I need to move G to (17,34)-(22,39) and then click (19,24).
To move G, I need to click on the target position. The position (17,34)-(22,39) corresponds to grid cell (18,35)-(21,38), which currently has an N token. Let me try clicking there.
